convention: Entrance padas use the traditional 32-pada door list, commonly traced to the Brihat Samhita, projected onto the compass. Each pada is 11.25°. Eight padas make one wall of 90°. Numbering runs clockwise and meets at the corners: East E1–E8 from 45° (northeast) to 135°, South S1–S8 from 135° to 225°, West W1–W8 from 225° to 315°, North N1–N8 from 315° (northwest) to 45°. Intervals are half-open. The start angle belongs to that pada, and the clockwise edge belongs to the next. 0° and 360° are the same heading and fall in N5 (Soma). 90° is E5 (Surya), 180° is S5 (Yama), 270° is W5 (Varuna). 45° is E1, 135° is S1, 225° is W1, 315° is N1. The eight classically favored padas are E3 Jayanta, E4 Indra, S4 Grihakshata, W4 Pushpadanta, W5 Varuna, N3 Mukhya, N4 Bhallata, and N5 Soma. S3 Vitatha and W3 Sugriva are marked neutral: many modern guides allow them, and the classical list does not praise them. A phone measures the direction you face, not a tape along the wall, so a pada here is the compass sector of that facing. Eight-point directions are 45° sectors with North centered on 0°, so North owns [337.5°, 22.5°). Sixteen zones are the app's existing 22.5° zones, also with North centered on 0° ([348.75°, 11.25°)). All of this is per traditional Vaastu guidelines, not a building instruction.

checks.bestNote: Best in the south, southwest, or west. Keep stairs out of the northeast and the exact center.

zones.name: North
zones.meaning: North is not the usual place for a staircase.
remedies: If a turn allows, let the heavier steps rise toward the south or west.
Use the space under the stairs for storage, not for a shrine.
Keep the northeast free of the stair.

checks.title: Mirror
checks.instructions: Stand in the middle of the room and point the phone at the mirror.
checks.bestNote: Best on a north or east wall. Avoid a mirror facing the bed or the main door.

zones.name: North
zones.meaning: A mirror on the north is a traditional placement.

zones.name: Northeast
zones.meaning: A mirror toward the northeast is workable if it does not face the bed.
remedies: North and east walls are the usual choice.
Keep it from facing the bed.

zones.name: East
zones.meaning: A mirror on the east is a traditional placement.

zones.name: Southeast
zones.meaning: A mirror toward the southeast is not the usual placement.
remedies: Prefer a north or east wall if the mirror can move.
Do not let it face the bed or the main door directly.
If it must stay, angle it aside, or cover it while you sleep.

checks.title: Television
checks.instructions: Stand in the middle of the room and point the phone at the television.
checks.bestNote: Best in the southeast or northwest of the room. Keep it out of the northeast.

zones.name: North
zones.meaning: North can hold a screen if the northeast corner stays clear.
remedies: Keep the screen out of the northeast corner.
Switch it off when nobody is watching, and tidy the cables.

zones.name: Northeast
zones.meaning: Northeast is not the usual place for a television.
remedies: The southeast or northwest of the room is the usual place for a screen.
Keep the television out of the northeast prayer corner.
A low, tidy stand is enough.

checks.title: Garden and tulsi
checks.instructions: Stand at the center of the home, or of the yard, and point the phone at the tulsi or the main plants.
checks.bestNote: Best in the north, northeast, or east. Tulsi is traditionally kept off the south.

zones.name: North
zones.meaning: North is a favored side for tulsi and a light garden.

zones.name: Northeast
zones.meaning: Northeast is a classical place for tulsi.

zones.name: East
zones.meaning: East suits tulsi and morning light on the plants.

zones.name: Southeast
zones.meaning: Southeast is not the usual place for tulsi.
remedies: Move a tulsi pot to the north, northeast, or east if you can.
Other shrubs can stay. Tulsi is the plant this check is about.
Keep the pot clean, and water it.
